references.name: Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk / Capital and Interest
references.connection: Provided the civilization-rate thesis quoted in the introduction

references.name: Richard Cantillon / Essai sur la Nature du Commerce en Général
references.connection: Early theorist of interest and money flows; context for 18th-century rate analysis

references.name: David Hume / Essays
references.connection: Argued low interest rates reflect abundance of capital, not policy — referenced in methodological discussions

references.name: Walter Bagehot / Lombard Street
references.desc: Editor, The Economist; Victorian-era financial commentator
references.connection: Classic analysis of the Bank of England's role; informs discussion of 19th-century English rate mechanism

references.name: John Maynard Keynes / General Theory
references.connection: Theory of the "liquidity trap" — relevant to Japan's and later Western near-zero rate environment

references.name: Charles Kindleberger / Manias, Panics and Crashes
references.connection: Documents how financial crises produce rate spikes; complements Homer's long-run rate framework

references.name: Paul Volcker / Federal Reserve Chairman 1979–1987
references.connection: His 1979–1982 rate shock is the book's most analyzed recent event — the turn of the secular rate cycle

references.name: Milton Friedman / A Monetary History of the United States
references.connection: Provides the theoretical framework for interpreting the Fed's role in the 1966–1981 great inflation
